title: Switch to Momentum Energy, Stay 30 Days for eGift Cards: $225 for Residential Electricity, $150 for Residential Gas @ Econnex
body:
Deal: Switch to Momentum Energy, Stay 30 Days for eGift Cards: $225 for Residential Electricity, $150 for Residential Gas @ Econnex

[TaurusHead] Although these guys always come through, the advertisement on these posts seem to be misleading, I mean it says stay for 30 days but in fact they want you to stay connected until the gift cards are on your way, and that takes 90 days.
[saminn] not sure if anything changed recently but have always made sure to stay for 30/45 days based on the terms from when I was connected to the new provider and not when I made the application and haven't missed a single GC
[Dan888] Same - I always change the provider after 45 days (just to make sure - and to get at least one bill) — i have always received my GC
[Nusername] Econnex’s T&Cs state that a customer is ineligible if “the customer does not meet the … provider eligibility requirements”.
The plan I’m being offered is Momentum Energy’s “Warm Welcome” plan. Its eligibility criteria ( https://www.momentumenergy.com.au/docs/default-source/terms-… ) state that “2. the Market Contract must be your first electricity Market Contract with us for the Supply Address (New Contract)”.
If you're only offered the Warm Welcome plan, I read this as being ineligible for the gift card if you've used Momentum energy before?
[Wiadro] Daily Supply Charge: 172.15c/day
Peak Usage: 26.62c/kWh
FIT: 3c/kWh
jesus what a bad deal
[prankster] That’s just how it is nowadays and most companies have similar pricing 😭
[Gavman] Depends. Definitely on the crap side. But that’s the trade off.
[bigbadboogieman] $1.7215 / day supply charge = $154.94 minimum fixed charge for 90 days. Feels like a rip-off when it used to be between $0.60 and $0.80 / day. Everything feels like a rip-off nowadays.
Edit: It's shit that the govt charges GST as if electricity is not a necessity in today's world.
[rooster7777] Yep… even cars! everything is a ripoff these days! a holden used to cost $2000!
Lucky there's a crapload more dollars in your wallet than "back then".
[bigbadboogieman] "Back then".. lolz. My friend not everyone in life is against you and not everyone is an old timer.
Here is a list of historical plan paperwork I have kept in my archive. I am a serial churner and currently waiting for an $800 rebate on a battery rewards plan.
Below just goes to show how we all got (profanity) under labour's energy policy while they created an illusion of "doing something"..
All price incl. GST:
01-Jul-2026: Supply charge c/day 147.994
08-Dec-2025: Supply charge c/day 102.850
02-Nov-2025: Supply charge c/day 102.003
08-Nov-2024: Supply charge c/day 72.193
19-May-2024: Supply charge c/day 88.121

20-Oct-2023: Supply charge c/day 81.810
28-Jul-2023: Supply charge c/day 86.625
02-Jun-2022: Supply charge c/day 71.500
[rooster7777] @bigbadboogieman: Thanks for the data.
You're the one that said "nowadays" not me young old timer.
I don't disagree that the supply charge component has increased significantly, and significantly more than the power use cost. With the plethora of suppliers around now, the permutations of supply/use costs are very widespread…. without the two side by side the real cost is hidden.
Speaking of old timers… I'm guessing you're regretting/ resisting the charge to renewable energy, and believe that we should be using coal with a trumpian burn baby burn mantra…. given that you specified labor's energy policy is the problem…. which is incredibly ironic while you state in the same post that you're waiting for an $800 battery related rebate.
Many people around the world are comfortable about paying higher energy costs to move to renewables, if that higher cost isn't going to windfall profits somewhere.
On the other hand, many folks around the world are NOT comfortable about paying higher energy costs for renewables, on the basis of either they don't give a rats about the world that they leave for future generations, or that they believe the earth is flat, and climate change is an embarrassingly obvious fantasy.
So my friend, are you one of the above two, or do you think something in the liberal toolkit would have done better? (keeping in mind turnbull, arguably the wisest and most scientifically aware of the coalition leaders… had his name on the huge snowy 2 forkup)
[bigbadboogieman] @rooster7777: Yes Labour's energy policy around hiking supply charges to the moon is a long term problem. There are reports that it could go up to $5 a day in 10 years time. Nothing wrong with renewables but letting these massive corporations that control supply infrastructure drill Aussies into the ground with profiteering hidden as inflation is absolutely ridiculous. The audacity is that they claimed electricity price reduction earlier this year as a win but reality was they reduced usage charges by 5% and increased supply charges between 25% to 50%.
Yes I got a battery because I am an OzBargainer and I got a good deal. I go where the rebates take me. Trust me these two things can be mutually exclusive.
[rooster7777] @bigbadboogieman: Fantastic sidestep from the question about your social responsibility as an energy consumer, why you are resistant to renewable energy cost.
There are reports that the earth is flat.
Since the industry of poles and wires and transformers and all that stuff has been separated from the smoke and mirrors of marketing, where the costs/ profits go is now a bit clearer… they aren't combined in an opaque blob.
I sympathise with your concern that the cost to supply power to a premise for a week is now in the ballpark of a cost of a takeaway coffee, though not very much as I have some idea of behind the scenes costs of maintanance crews, emergency response crews, requirement to provide services in uneconomic scenarios meaning costs must be balanced across all users etc… but yes, all labor's fault.
By the way, if you're going to keep slagging off the labor party that of course is your right (I do too, for what I consider far more valid reasons than blaming them for supply power costs)… but you should at least learn how to spell that big word properly for credibility sake.
[rooster7777] if its peak usage charge is 27c/kwh in SA that's forken cheap… supply charges are all over the place from about $1…. but are dwarfed by useage charges nope…in sa it's $1.67/day and 37c/KWh which is still a cheap useage charge.

[prankster] @paul11: Surprised the company hasn’t updated you to the latest (increased) rates coz $0.80 for supply fee is a bargain with today’s prices
[prodnus] Only offered electricity in the north west of Sydney for some reason. No gas options. Is this the same for others in NSW?
[TThomas] I had the opposite, only offering me gas in Melb outer east…
[jimbler] I've got a $150 cashback offer from NAB Goodies for signing up with Momentum and staying a month. Anyone else got that and thinking of doing this as well? Can they be combined?
You can get an extra $100 ($250 total) if you stay for 12 months, but not interested in doing that. Just want the $150 and get out ASAP after a month.
https://i.imgur.com/hCeziue.jpeg
https://i.imgur.com/HrB5EJn.jpeg
[Etherkai] From what I can tell, it can't be done. The link in my NAB Goodies takes me directly to the Momentum Energy website whereas this offer is via Econnex with no option to enter the NAB unique offer code in the sign-up process.
